# Results — Study 604 (Month-End Rebalancing Flows)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(institutional folklore, formalised by Etula-Rinne-Suominen-Vaittinen's *Dash for Cash* and the
target-date/pension rebalancing literature) — **after a month when stocks trounce bonds,
calendar rebalancers sell equities into month-end, and the pressure reverses in the first days
of the new month** — measured on SPY vs a spliced Aggregate-bond leg (VBMFX before 2003-09-30,
AGG after — the same Bloomberg Aggregate index; splice done in RETURN space) from yfinance
total-return closes. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (June 2026 is the last complete month).
Fingerprint `3efe1915419d`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | SPY + AGG + VBMFX **total-return** (auto-adjusted) closes, 8,430 rows, 1993-01-04 → 2026-06-30 (yfinance, no key) |
| Bond splice | the research plan sketched TLT pre-2003; TLT only reaches 2002-07 and is a 20+yr *long-duration* fund — a poor stand-in for the policy-mix bond leg. We splice **VBMFX → AGG at 2003-09-30** instead: VBMFX tracks the *same* Aggregate index and covers the whole SPY era. Splice in **return space** (no level stitching) |
| Sample | 8,410 daily return sessions, 1993-02-01 → 2026-06-30; **401 complete months** (1993-02 → 2026-06) |
| Windows | last **3** / first **3** trading days of each month; conditioning = month-to-date equity-minus-bond cumulative-return gap through the close **3 days before month-end** (`gap_pre`, strictly prior to the last-3 window) or the full-month gap (`gap_full`, known at the month-end close, strictly prior to the first-3 window) |
| Tests | quintile splits with **Welch t** (non-overlapping monthly windows — plain t's are the right tool); a **permutation placebo** (gap shuffled across months) averaged over **20 seeds × 2,000 draws**; the tradability daily stream gets a **Newey-West (HAC, 5 lags) t** |
| Execution / costs | signals use only closes already printed; entry at the signal close, first return earned the next session — exactly **one execution lag**. Trade costs 2 / 5 bps **one-way × NAV per leg**, 8 one-way tickets per event (open pair + month-end flip at 2× notional + close); the short leg pays **30 bps/yr borrow** pro-rata |
| Survivorship | none — broad index vehicles (SPY / AGG / VBMFX), no panel selection |

## Leg 1 — the sell-the-winner leg (last-3-day spread | MTD gap)

The flow story's first prediction: after stocks trounce bonds month-to-date, the last-3-day
equity-minus-bond spread should be **negative** (rebalancers sell the winner).

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| top-gap quintile (mean MTD gap **+6.22%**) | **−46.53 bps** over the last 3 days · one-sample *t* = **−2.88** (n = 81) |
| bottom-gap quintile (gap −5.32%) | +11.58 bps · *t* = +0.36 (n = 81) |
| unconditional last-3 spread | **−19.13 bps** · *t* = −2.07 (n = 401) |
| **top-minus-bottom** | **−58.11 bps** · Welch *t* = **−1.60** · top-vs-unconditional Welch *t* = −1.47 |
| permutation placebo (20 seeds × 2,000 draws) | **p = 0.0225** [0.0175, 0.0300] |

The **level** clears the bar: in top-gap months equities lag bonds by −46.5 bps over the final
three sessions (*t* = −2.88), the dose-response is monotone across quintiles (+11.6 → −46.5
bps), and a random re-tagging of months only beats it ~2.3% of the time. But the **purely
conditional differential** (top vs bottom, the part that distinguishes flows from a plain
month-end drift) reads Welch *t* = −1.60 — below the bar on the pre-registered 3-day window
(it clears at k = 4: Welch *t* = −3.61; see robustness).

## Leg 2 — the reversal leg (first-3-day spread | prior full-month gap)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| top-gap quintile | +50.67 bps · *t* = +2.26 (n = 80) |
| bottom-gap quintile | +13.96 bps · *t* = +0.44 |
| unconditional first-3 spread | **+33.54 bps** · *t* = **+3.28** (n = 400) |
| **top-minus-bottom** | +36.70 bps · Welch *t* = **+0.95** |
| permutation placebo | **p = 0.1317** [0.1240, 0.1435] |

The first-days equity pop is **real but unconditional**: +33.5 bps of spread with *t* = +3.28
regardless of the prior gap. The gap-conditionality the flow story demands is absent (Welch
*t* = +0.95, placebo p ≈ 0.13, and the dose-response is flat: Q2 = +45.8 bps vs Q5 = +50.7 bps).
This leg is the turn-of-the-month effect wearing a rebalancing costume.

| quintile | mean MTD gap | last-3 spread (bps) | t | first-3 spread (bps) | t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 | −5.32% | +11.58 | +0.36 | +13.96 | +0.44 |
| Q2 | −0.92% | +2.22 | +0.14 | +45.78 | +2.00 |
| Q3 | +1.20% | −19.75 | −1.19 | +29.96 | +1.54 |
| Q4 | +2.87% | −43.63 | −2.75 | +27.33 | +1.81 |
| Q5 | +6.22% | **−46.45** | **−2.84** | +50.67 | +2.26 |

Monotone on the sell leg; flat on the reversal leg.

## Era split

| era | SELL: top (t) | SELL: diff, Welch t | REV: top (t) | REV: diff, Welch t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| pre-AGG (1993–2003-09) | −69.18 bps (−1.95) | −0.99 bps, −0.01 | +3.52 bps (+0.08) | −29.92 bps, −0.38 |
| 2004–2015 | −50.99 bps (−2.17) | **−116.71 bps, −2.14** | **+135.50 bps (+5.22)** | **+180.14 bps, +3.22** |
| 2016+ | −12.07 bps (−0.57) | −50.71 bps, −0.95 | −8.54 bps (−0.24) | −92.89 bps, **−1.52** (flipped) |

The conditional flow effect was a **2004–2015 phenomenon** — both legs cleared the bar there —
and has faded (sell leg) or **flipped sign** (reversal leg) since 2016, exactly the footprint of
an arbitraged-away flow.

| k | SELL top (t) | SELL diff Welch t | REV top (t) | REV diff Welch t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 | −42.39 bps (−2.74) | −1.90 | +61.18 bps (+3.61) | +1.96 |
| **3 (headline)** | **−46.53 bps (−2.88)** | **−1.60** | **+50.67 bps (+2.26)** | **+0.95** |
| 4 | −55.51 bps (−3.13) | **−3.61** | +66.10 bps (+2.82) | +1.72 |

The sell-leg **level** clears at every window (*t* = −2.7 to −3.1); the conditional differential
clears only at k = 4 — we keep the pre-registered k = 3 headline and report this honestly rather
than shop the window.

## Tradability — the expanding-quintile flow trade

When `gap_pre` exceeds the 80th percentile of all **prior** months (expanding threshold, 60-month
burn-in — no full-sample snooping): short SPY / long AGG over the last 3 days, flip long SPY /
short AGG over the first 3 days. 8 one-way tickets per event; short leg pays 30 bps/yr borrow.

| setting | events | active days | gross | net | HAC t (net, active days) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 bps/leg | 70 | 5.0% | +2.06%/yr | **+1.72%/yr** | **+2.52** |
| 5 bps/leg | 70 | 5.0% | +2.06%/yr | +1.22%/yr | +1.78 |
| 1993–2015 only (2 bps) | 46 | | | **+2.90%/yr** | **+3.42** |
| 2016–2026 only (2 bps, 24m burn-in) | 26 | | | **−0.07%/yr** | −0.07 |

Per-event gross **+98.1 bps** vs 16 bps of tickets at 2 bps/leg. The trade clears the bar on the
full tape at 2 bps — but it is a **1993–2015 phenomenon** that has earned **nothing since 2016**
and drops below the bar at 5 bps/leg. Real once, decayed and regime-dependent → **FRAGILE**.

## Third axis — is the turn-of-the-month (study 89) just this in disguise?

If study [89-turn-of-the-month](../../89-turn-of-the-month/)'s unconditional first-days drift
were really rebalancing flows, it should concentrate in big-gap months and vanish when the prior
month's equity-bond gap is small (nothing to rebalance).

| slice | first-3-day SPY drift | t |
|---|--:|--:|
| unconditional (all 400 months) | +34.41 bps | +3.55 |
| **middle 3 gap-quintiles (no rebalancing pressure)** | **+36.35 bps** | **+3.45** (n = 240) |
| top gap quintile | +43.88 bps | +2.05 |
| bottom gap quintile | +19.12 bps | +0.64 |
| extremes-vs-middle Welch t | | **−0.23** (n_ext = 160) |

The TOM drift is **fully intact** in the middle quintiles — months where the prior equity-bond
gap was near zero and rebalancers had nothing to do — and the extremes are statistically
indistinguishable from the middle. **Turn-of-the-month is NOT rebalancing flows in disguise** —
BUSTED.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic two-asset random walk with a **planted** gap-conditional flow reversal
(`data.synthetic_world`, knob `edge`):

| world | SELL diff Welch t | REV diff Welch t | flow trade (2 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0, **20 seeds**) | mean **−0.04**, sd 0.59, max \|t\| = 1.79 — **0 of 20** clear \|t\| ≥ 2 | | seed 604: net +0.04%/yr, HAC t = +0.07 |
| planted 100 bps reversal (seed 604) | **−9.26** | **+5.66** | net **+4.35%/yr**, HAC t = **+7.04** |

The detector stays quiet on 20 independent null worlds and lights up hard on a planted flow.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited to support the real-tape stamps.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** *Real on the sell-the-winner leg · Weak on the reversal leg.* After
  equity-rich months the last-3-day equity-bond spread is **−46.5 bps** (one-sample
  *t* = **−2.88**), monotone in the gap, permutation placebo **p ≈ 0.022** — but the purely
  conditional top-vs-bottom differential misses on the pre-registered 3-day window (Welch
  *t* = −1.60; clears at k = 4). The reversal leg's first-days pop (+33.5 bps, *t* = +3.28) is
  **unconditional** — no gap dose-response (Welch *t* = +0.95, placebo p ≈ 0.13). No
  survivorship (broad index vehicles).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The expanding-threshold flow trade nets **+1.72%/yr** at 2 bps/leg
  (HAC *t* = +2.52, 5% of days at risk) — but it is a **1993–2015 phenomenon** (+2.90%/yr,
  *t* = 3.42) that has earned **−0.07%/yr since 2016** and drops below the bar at 5 bps/leg
  (*t* = 1.78). Real once, decayed.
- **"Is turn-of-the-month just this in disguise?" — BUSTED.** The TOM drift survives at full
  strength (+36.35 bps, *t* = 3.45) exactly where rebalancing pressure is absent (middle gap
  quintiles); extremes-vs-middle Welch *t* = −0.23. Study 89's calendar drift and this study's
  conditional flow are **different animals**.
